clue.text: Go to university — oddly, full houses reserved

parts.note: to have a go at something is to have a bash at it

indicators.note: to house is to hold inside, so the picked letters close around the university letter
the odd-numbered letters, first and third, are taken from the word full

explanation.surface: A student off to college finds every hall of residence already booked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes F and L from 'full', and 'houses' puts U between them to give FUL after BASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a shy, retiring person who holds back in company.

clue.text: Total initially missing in oil company's accident

indicators.note: the shortened total sits within the oil company's two letters

parts.note: BP is the British oil company

indicators.note: the opening letter is dropped from the word for a total

parts.note: a total is a sum

explanation.surface: A French oil firm's name turns up in a report on another oil company's mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: Total is also a French oil company, which pulls the eye toward company names; here it just means SUM, which loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump is a minor collision, as with a car, so a small accident.

clue.text: Carrier of baby grand cuts arm — sore toe hurt badly

indicators.note: the single letter cuts into the rearranged letters, sitting inside them
something done badly comes out all wrong, so these four words' letters are rearranged

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A piano is moved and its mover ends up with a cut arm and a sore toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baby grand' reads as a piano, but 'Carrier of baby' is the definition and 'grand' gives G, which 'cuts' into the anagram of ARM SORE TOE HURT.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who bears a child for someone else literally carries their baby.

clue.text: Loud Mel B raging over a light drink

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: a raging person is all over the place, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; she is Scary Spice of the Spice Girls

explanation.surface: Mel B of the Spice Girls loudly rages while someone offers her a weak drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light drink' is not a low-alcohol drink: read 'light' as a verb, to set brandy or another spirit on food alight. The anagram is of MEL B and A.
explanation.definitionFit: To flambé food is to pour spirit over it and set fire to it, so you ignite liquor.

clue.text: Shot up large old boy's bottom

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
OB stands for old boy, a former pupil
a bed is the bottom of a river or the sea

explanation.surface: A big former pupil gets a shot on the behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball that is lobbed is hit high into the air in an arc.

clue.text: Sole scourers — cat without tail around its prey?

indicators.note: the shortened cat word goes around the prey word
the cat word loses its final letter

parts.note: puss is an informal word for a cat
mice are what a cat hunts

explanation.surface: A cat that has lost its tail is circling the creatures it hunts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' is the underside of the foot, not the fish, and 'scourers' are the stones used to rub hard skin there.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice stones are porous volcanic rocks rubbed on the feet to remove hard skin.

clue.text: Shells protect other Ninja Turtles: Leonardo and Rafael initially damaged part of theirs?

indicators.note: damaged things are bent out of shape, so the picked letters are rearranged
the first letter of each of the eight words is taken

parts.words: Shells protect other Ninja Turtles: Leonardo and Rafael

explanation.surface: Two of the cartoon Ninja Turtles have hurt their protective shells while defending the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters S P O N T L A R, and 'damaged' rearranges them. 'theirs' means the turtles', so the definition is part of a turtle's shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastron is the flat underside section of a turtle or tortoise shell.

clue.text: Girl Power — stop waste

parts.note: miss is a word for a girl or young woman
P is the symbol for power in physics
to stop something is to end it

explanation.surface: The Spice Girls' slogan of girl power is told to come to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl Power' was the Spice Girls' catchphrase, which ties the clue to the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To misspend money or time is to waste it on the wrong things.

clue.text: Form of struggle in Africa, where calm is shattered

indicators.note: a shattered thing lies in pieces, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A peaceful part of Africa is disturbed by a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes AFRICA, WHERE and CALM together.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfare using poison gas and toxic substances is one kind of armed conflict.

clue.text: Stalk one of 12 — hot stuff

parts.note: a stem is the stalk of a plant
Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice, a member of the Spice Girls at 12 down

explanation.surface: A stem from a plant belongs to one group of hot foods.
explanation.walkthrough: The '12' points to the Spice Girls answer at 12 down, whose members had nicknames such as Ginger.
explanation.definitionFit: Preserved root of the spice plant, kept in syrup, is pungent and fiery on the tongue.

clue.text: Musical's lead song — this one?

indicators.note: the lead letter of a word is its first one

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: Asking whether a show's main number is the one being described.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: 'Maria' is a leading song from West Side Story.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated number sung by Tony in West Side Story, named after the heroine.

clue.text: Britain behind — that is concerning for supporter

parts.note: BR is a short form for Britain or British
ass is the American word for the backside
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A remark about Britain's backside, apparently concerning something that holds it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' sounds like a fan but is an undergarment that supports the bust.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra is a garment that supports a woman's breasts.

clue.text: Rolling Stones cut LP — iPod bug playing two notes at once

indicators.note: to roll something around is to tumble it, so all these letters are mixed together
a cut word is trimmed, here losing its final letter

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones record an album, but an iPod glitch spoils it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stones' reads as the band, but 'Rolling' is the anagram signal for STONE (Stones 'cut' of its S), LP, IPOD and BUG.
explanation.definitionFit: On a violin or similar instrument, bowing two strings together to sound a pair of pitches.

clue.text: Mistakes turning up — cold, horrible Geri splitting band

indicators.note: the inserted letters split the reversed word apart
in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: slips are small mistakes
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: something horrible is mangled, so the name's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A band breaks up after errors, a frosty atmosphere and Geri behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: SPILS is SLIPS turned up; C and EGIR (an anagram of GERI) go into it. Geri Halliwell famously left the band in 1998.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1990s British pop group, a manufactured girl group of five singers.

clue.text: Buggy — no round in middle of golf tournament?

indicators.note: the round thing is dropped entirely from the event's name
the letter removed sits at the centre of the tournament's name

parts.note: a pro-am is a golf event pairing professionals with amateurs
O is round, the shape of a ring

explanation.surface: A golf event loses a round halfway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buggy' suggests a golf cart, fitting the surface, but it is a baby's pushchair. A PRO-AM is a tournament for professionals and amateurs together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pram is a wheeled carriage pushed along with a baby inside.

clue.text: Well, peak with sex change?

indicators.note: male becomes female, so the letter for male is swapped for the letter for female

parts.note: a mountain is a peak

explanation.surface: Asking if a mountain could be all right after changing gender.
explanation.walkthrough: M (male) is replaced by F (female). 'Well' reads as an adverb but is the noun, a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring or source from which water flows, as in the old sense of a well.

clue.text: Delay while parking over street, just in time

indicators.note: the delay word stretches over the street letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a lag is a delay
as can mean while, at the same time
P is the road-sign symbol for parking

explanation.surface: Someone is held up while parking, but makes it in the nick of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means one piece spans the other, not a reversal; 'just in time' is the definition, not part of the delay story.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-gasp effort or goal comes at the very final moment before it is too late.

clue.text: Dancer upset popular judge governing on satellite

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word over so it reads upwards

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a party in power is said to be in
Sky is the British satellite television broadcaster

explanation.surface: A celebrity judge on a satellite TV dance show is overruled.
explanation.walkthrough: Vaslav Nijinsky was the great Russian ballet dancer; the surface suggests a TV talent show.
explanation.definitionFit: Nijinsky was a famous Russian ballet star of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: One climbs over it — a member of 12 second

indicators.note: turned over means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Mel C, Sporty Spice, was one of the Spice Girls at 12 down

explanation.surface: A climber goes over the top, followed by one of the band shortly after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses IT, A and MELC to give CLEMATI, then S for second.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is a vine that climbs up walls and trellises.

clue.text: Precious time with baby

parts.note: wee means tiny, and Emma Bunton was Baby Spice

explanation.surface: Time spent with an infant is treasured.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-refined, affectedly dainty or sweet in a cloying way.

clue.text: Figures include drink

parts.note: to add something is to include it
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Numbers come with a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' reads as numbers, but it is the verb in 'that figures', meaning it makes sense.
explanation.definitionFit: When something makes sense, people say it figures, or that it computes logically.

clue.text: Awards no marks

parts.note: O is a nought, meaning none
scars are marks left on skin

explanation.surface: Prizes given with no points scored.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Awards for film, the gold statuettes handed out in Hollywood.

clue.text: Good line wasted by Democrat — America to go for developing business

parts.note: a row is a line
wasted means emaciated, very thin
D is short for Democrat in US politics
US is the United States
a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: A fine political line is eroded by a Democrat as America makes an attempt at developing industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector of the economy that is expanding fast is a booming one.

clue.text: Top footballer once

definitions.meaning: George ... was a celebrated Manchester United and Northern Ireland player of the 1960s

explanation.definitionFit: Supreme or finest; also the surname of a famous Northern Irish footballer of the past.

clue.text: Trains for show on late transport

parts.note: re means on, concerning
hearses carry the late, the dead

explanation.surface: Railway services for a performance run behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, not delayed, so the transport is a funeral vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a performance before the actual one is to prepare for a show.

clue.text: Saw commercial season

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a season or age is a long period

explanation.surface: Someone spotted an advert during the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see, but is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saying or proverb is called a saw.

clue.text: Bad-tempered — wearing sporty pants initially …

indicators.note: the letters are worn down and rearranged, a jumbling sign here
only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone sulks about having to wear sporty trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: SPORTY with P, the first letter of 'pants', is rearranged. Sporty Spice was Mel C's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in a strop is sulky and irritable, easily angered.

clue.text: … most classy model — way over height

indicators.note: the model word lies over the height letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to pose is to model for a picture
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: The smartest model stands tall on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Posh Spice was Victoria Beckham's nickname in the Spice Girls, the theme band at 12 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh means upper-class or smart, and this is its superlative form.
